analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 35-42, 109-148, 250-259, 365-372) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new GLM5Next section at head lines 71-310, reasoning-parser text near 902-959, MiMo tool-schema text near 1225-1250, GLM tool-parser and shutdown logging text near 1498-1505). No source, config or endpoint changes are in the supplied material, so I could not check that the docs match the code.

Security-relevant claims I checked against the threat model:
- Prefix cache (T-041): media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture. The GLM execution policy is part of the encrypted checkpoint storage identity. The SSD tier's typed refusal reason reaches only local /metrics. None of this widens the at-rest or TTFT-oracle surface.
- Memory and availability (T-010, T-029, T-016, TB-007): the docs describe fail-closed retention of unproven native retirement, quarantine of GLM work only, charging of retained bytes into fleet KV budgets, and pre-stream 503 capacity refusals. These are stated as hardening, not as a weakened control.
- Prompt and tool handling (TB-002, A-001): MiMo restores original tool schemas only after the loaded model resolves to exact mimo_v2, and client-supplied reserved schema metadata is rejected. The GLM parser withholds the tool suffix and caps it at 1 MiB, and a malformed suffix fails before any text or call is published.
- Logging (A-001): void bridge shutdown now logs a fixed diagnostic without the error payload, which reduces leakage.
- Responses retention: the docs state that the SDK response-object store has no eviction matching the history LRU. This is a documented application-memory and DoS caveat, not a regression. Whether it needs a threat-model entry depends on code outside the supplied evidence.

No coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest or authorization behavior is touched. These are doc assertions about code I was not given, so no finding is raised. Later passes should confirm that the claimed GLM refusal and ownership behavior matches the code if code diffs appear in other batches.
